summary: A work-led site for a photographer, architecture / interiors / design practice or photo studio: the work leads, each project gets its own case page, and an about + contact page closes the sale. Studios that sell fixed packages add a pricing page with a package builder and a booking page.

pages.purpose: Show the work within one screen and let the visitor browse it by discipline, then point to the projects, the person or studio behind them and the way to commission.

sections.purpose: The name (or studio name) as the image: oversized type, what they do, where they work and whether they are taking work now.
alternatives: image: a single framed hero photograph or model shot with a caption line, for an architecture practice or a photo studio
fields: Availability line (booking from / taking commissions from)
Up to three quick facts (projects, years active, formats or people)
Primary action (commission / book / build a package)
sections.notes: Keep the hero typographic for a solo photographer; for a practice, a captioned hero figure (number, caption, credit) reads like a drawing sheet. Only one scroll-linked effect at most (a slow parallax on the hero image).

sections.purpose: The work itself: a filterable wall of images or a sequence of captioned plates linking to each project.
alternatives: gallery-section: a fixed mosaic of recent work with captions, for a studio that sells sessions rather than projects
media-text: alternating large plates with a caption block (place, type, area, status, year) for an architecture or interiors practice
fields: Selected images with width, height and real alt text
sections.notes: Masonry wall with a category filter (pill tabs with counts) that opens in a lightbox with thumbnails. Practices alternate plate sizes and positions across a 12-column grid so the page never settles into a card grid.

sections.purpose: Every project as one row, so a visitor can scan the whole body of work and open any case page.
alternatives: list-layout: a plain ruled list when there are fewer than ten projects
fields: Area and status: built, on site, in design, unbuilt (practices)
sections.notes: A register of hairline rows, newest first, with a typology filter and a live count ('n of m projects'). Rows link only when a case page exists. A cover preview that follows the cursor is a nice extra but pointer-only: keep every row a plain link and show a thumbnail in the row on touch screens.

sections.purpose: What the practice does and the numbers behind it.
fields: Services or kinds of work, each with one line

sections.purpose: For a hireable photo studio: the room and its kit (size, light, backdrops, changing room).
Preset packages as numbered frames, each opening the package builder pre-filled.
alternatives: feature-grid: packages described without prices when every job is quoted
fields: What is included (studio hours, edited images, people)

sections.purpose: Awards, publications, exhibitions or selected clients as credibility.
alternatives: logo-strip: when clients allow their logos to be shown
testimonials: quotes from clients for a studio that sells sessions

sections.purpose: The photographer or the people behind the studio.
A short statement and bio leading to about and contact, plus when new work is accepted.

pages.purpose: The full work wall and project index when the home page only shows a selection.

sections.purpose: Title and a line on what is included (commissioned and personal, period covered).
All images, filterable by discipline, opening in the lightbox.
fields: Images with alt text and captions

sections.purpose: Every project as a row linking to its case page.
fields: Project title, client type, discipline, year

pages.purpose: One case story per project: the facts, the cover, the story, the rest of the series or the drawings, credits and the next project.

sections.purpose: Breadcrumb, project number of total, title, a one-paragraph summary and the facts.
sections.notes: Facts sit in a ruled box like a drawing title block.

sections.purpose: The cover image across the page.
Brief, approach and result as three numbered columns; practices interleave text blocks with figures and plans.
alternatives: rich-text-section: a longer narrative with figures for an architecture project
section-nav: a sticky margin list of numbered figure captions that tracks the figure in view and jumps to it
sections.notes: In the margin-caption variant, every caption is listed in a sticky margin; the caption of the figure in view is marked with aria-current and choosing one scrolls to its figure (smooth only without reduced motion).

sections.purpose: The rest of the series as a masonry wall that opens in the lightbox.
Who worked on it and the technical facts.
fields: Credit label and value pairs (editor, client, designer, camera, consultants, contractor)

sections.purpose: A large link to the next project, so the visitor keeps going.

pages.purpose: For studios with fixed prices: presets, and a builder that turns choices into a live quote carried over to booking.

sections.purpose: What a package contains and how the price is built.
Preset starting points, each loading the builder.
Build a session: session type, studio time, edited images, people (for headshots) and extras, with a live quote beside it.
fields: Session types with base price, included hours and images
Price per extra hour and per extra image
Extras with flat price or percentage (make-up, stylist, backdrop, raw files, prints, rush delivery)
sections.notes: Numbered steps on the left, a sticky receipt on the right: line items, subtotal, VAT, total, deposit and delivery time. The total is announced in a polite live region. Switching the session type resets hours, images and people to that session's base. 'Book this package' carries the build to the booking page and survives a language switch.

pages.purpose: Hold a date: pick a day and start time, leave details, accept the terms; the package summary and deposit stay in view.

sections.purpose: How holding a date works (how long it is held, how the deposit is paid).
Choose a day on the calendar, then an available start time.
alternatives: scheduler: when the studio runs several rooms or photographers
sections.notes: Days and start times are buttons with full date labels; fully booked days say so and offer another day.

sections.purpose: Contact details, the brief and the booking terms.
alternatives: contact-form: a plain enquiry when the studio confirms by hand
fields: Booking terms: deposit refund window, reschedule rule
sections.notes: Validate on submit with an error summary; the confirmation is a status region with the date, the deposit amount and a reference.

sections.purpose: The chosen package, total and deposit beside the form, with a link back to change it.
sections.notes: If no package was built, show the default session and say it can be changed.

pages.purpose: Who is behind the work, how a commission runs, clients and shows, and the enquiry form.

sections.purpose: A titled introduction: who, where, since when.
How they work beside a portrait or studio photo, with the practical terms.
fields: How a commission starts and runs
Rate basis (day rate, licensing per use / territory / term) if published
Portrait or studio photo with alt text

sections.purpose: The people in the studio.
fields: Name, role and specialty per person

sections.purpose: How a commission runs, step by step.
fields: Steps from first conversation to handover, with what happens in each

sections.purpose: Selected clients by sector and exhibitions by year.
Address, opening hours and how to get there, for a studio visitors come to.
Practical questions (delivery time, usage rights, what to bring, cancellations).
The enquiry form with the kind of work as a choice and reply expectations.
fields: Kinds of enquiry (commission, licensing an existing image, print sale, other)

content: Selected images or project photographs, each with width, height and real alt text
Project list: title, client or client type, discipline / typology, year, place, status
Per project: summary, brief, approach, result, credits and the further images or drawings
Short statement of approach and biography (or studio history)
Availability: from when new work is booked
Selected clients, awards, publications or exhibitions
Team members with roles and portraits (studios)
How a commission runs, and what the client receives
Image licensing terms and rate basis, if published
For bookable studios: session types, inclusions, extras, prices, VAT, deposit and delivery times
For bookable studios: opening hours, closed days, address, booking and cancellation terms
Contact email, phone and reply time

styles.name: type-led gallery
styles.why: Oversized grotesk name, square images, mono eyebrows and one warm accent; the photographs carry all the colour. Suits a solo photographer or illustrator.

styles.name: drawing sheet
styles.why: Light page on a visible 12-column grid, light-weight large headings, hairline rules, numbered figures and mono captions; slow linear reveals. Suits architecture, interiors and design practices.

styles.name: darkroom mono
styles.why: Black and white only, a wide mono for headlines and numbers, crop marks and frame counters, near-square corners. Suits a photo studio selling sessions and room hire.

pitfalls: Every image needs meaningful alt text; the lightbox must trap focus, close on Escape and return focus to the image that opened it.
Hover-only effects (cursor-following cover previews, hover captions) must have a keyboard and touch equivalent; the project list stays usable as plain links.
Huge unoptimised images: give width and height, serve sized variants and only prioritise the hero.
Showing client names, logos or recognisable people without permission or a model release; state image licensing terms rather than implying images are free to use.
Prices shown without VAT or without saying what is included, and deposits without refund and reschedule terms next to the button.
A live quote that is not announced: put the total in a polite status region and keep it in sync with the booking summary.
Category filters that hide everything or lose state on language switch; show counts and keep the choice.
Decorative extras (grid overlays, keyboard shortcuts) presented as if required to use the site.
